notes: The coordinates in plans-v1 (29.0667, 76.5667) lie about 25 km east of the site. The report itself (Chapter II) gives 29 deg 02' 22" N, 76 deg 18' 21" E, and Fig. 7 gives Datum Point 2 as 29 deg 02' 26" N, 76 deg 18' 30" E; the mound was found 100-200 m from these points, south of the Meham road west of a road junction, as a group of light terraced fields between a north-south field boundary on the east and a foot track on the west. Fig. 19's caption says 'Trench 3', but its grid labels 1A-1H and its stepped outline are those of the 43 trenches opened in Locality 1 in 2007-08 that the text of Chapter III lists, and Fig. 7 draws the same stepped outline as 'Locality 1 / Trench 1'; all ten corners of that outline are the class P link. Fig. 7 is a colour contour map; its terraces are field and ownership units (the text says Locality 2 has a different owner), so terrace edges were matched to field boundaries in the October 2011 capture, the closest in time to the survey. Only Wayback release 4230 (capture 2011-10-04) at zoom 17 shows the terraces; zoom 18 tiles exist only from 2021, after the fields were re-laid. Capture dates come from each release's Wayback metadata layer (read as month/day/year). The fitted scale of the Fig. 7 link agrees with its scale bar to 0.2 per cent although the scale was not constrained, which supports the identification of the ditch and the block corners. No statement of a wall's or a town's orientation was seen in the parts of the report read (Chapters II and III, figure captions). Seen without opening any file: the session's starting git status, and a later `git status` run to confirm which files I had written, list untracked conjecture files whose names state working hypotheses about town orientation (knowledge/conjectures/C-0015-towns-laid-out-on-star-settings.md and C-0016-plains-cities-on-true-north.md). They give no value for any plan, and I chose no point with them in mind.
